Year 7 Science · Unit plan

Unit: Space

3 weeks · 6 core lessons and the topic test, plus optional Lesson 4 and above-level Lessons 8–10 · Victorian Curriculum F–10 v2.0

Students model the Earth–Sun–Moon system to explain day and night, seasons, the Moon’s phases, eclipses and tides, then move out into the solar system. They evaluate the benefits, risks and sustainability of space technology, and study Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander astronomy as science built over tens of thousands of years of observation on Country. Lessons 8–10 take a ready class above level: the search for life, gravity and orbits, and stars and starlight.

Achievement standard · Levels 7–8

  • Science Understanding. Explain how cyclic changes in the relative positions of Earth, the Sun and the Moon cause predictable phenomena on Earth, including day and night, seasons, the Moon’s phases, eclipses and tides.
  • Science Inquiry. Organise data in tables, graphs, models and mathematical relationships; analyse patterns, trends and anomalies.
  • Science as a Human Endeavour. Explain how new evidence can change scientific models (models of the solar system); examine how different perspectives and worldviews contribute to scientific knowledge (Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander astronomy); discuss the considerations in responses to a socio-scientific issue (space debris); analyse how science communication shapes viewpoints, policies and regulations.

Content descriptors

VC2S8U12
Cyclic changes in the relative positions of Earth, the Sun and the Moon cause eclipses and predictable phenomena on Earth, including seasons and tides
VC2S8H01
Scientific knowledge, including models and theories, can change because of new evidence
VC2S8H02
Multidisciplinary endeavours to advance scientific knowledge draw on people’s different perspectives and worldviews
VC2S8H03
Proposed scientific responses to socio-scientific issues impact society and involve ethical, environmental, social and economic considerations
VC2S8H04
Science communication shapes individual viewpoints, community policies and regulations
VC2S8U11
Rock-cycle processes occur over different timescales; rock properties reflect their formation — Lesson 4 (optional) only
VC2S8I04–I05
Science inquiry — organising data in tables, graphs, models and mathematical relationships (I04); analysing patterns, trends and anomalies (I05)
VC2S8U14
Balanced and unbalanced forces, including gravitational force — the Year 7–8 entry point for Lesson 9
VC2S10U12
Levels 9–10, above level — space exploration and the challenges of living away from Earth
VC2S10U13
Levels 9–10, above level — galaxies, stars, solar systems and black holes; the big bang theory
VC2S10U14
Levels 9–10, above level — wave models and the electromagnetic spectrum
VC2S10U17
Levels 9–10, above level — Newton’s laws applied to orbits

Prepare for learning

  • Lesson 1 entry task: rank Earth, Moon, Sun and other objects by size.
  • Every deck from Lesson 2 opens with a spaced retrieval warm-up.

Review and reflect

  • Booklet sections checked in class; Stile check-ins; exit passes.
  • The Retrieval Quiz — 217 questions, filter by lesson — for revision.

Modifications for DI and IEPs

  • Structure tasks in §1 are label-the-diagram rather than blank recall; phases are taught from the visualiser before the diagram; planet mnemonics on the slide.
  • The milestone task is cut-and-arrange; the debris calculation comes with the formula and one worked substitution.
  • Revision runs off the Retrieval Quiz filtered to the weakest lessons.

Extension

  • Lessons 8–10 (above level, VC2S10U12–U14, U17), behind the violet divider in the booklet.
  • Lesson 7 You do: reply to “Aboriginal astronomy can’t be reliable science because it isn’t written down”; the Lesson 6 mission brief.

Print the whole thing

  • Lesson Booklet 1 — core Lessons 1–7 (A5, 76 pp.)
  • Lesson Booklet 2 — above-level Lessons 8–10 (A5, 40 pp.)
  • Experiment Booklet — Experiments 1–2 (A4, 27 pp.)

Each lesson row links its own booklet pages for printing one section at a time.

  • Lesson 4 (Reading the Rocks) is optional — the unit is coherent without it, and §3 is not assessed.
  • Lessons 8–10 sit above the Year 7 level — the core unit is complete without them; run them with a ready class or as individual extension.

Our solar system

6

Space technology and sustainability

  • Outline key milestones in space exploration; describe crewed, robotic and telescope missions and Australia’s contributions.
  • Explain how space debris accumulates and the Kessler syndrome; evaluate the sustainability of orbital activity (VC2S8H03).
  • Explain how communicating the science of space debris shapes public views and space regulations (VC2S8H04).

I can evaluate the benefits and risks of a space mission, and propose a debris-management response with its trade-offs.
